3149.name: Hippocrates

3150.quote: Art is permitted to survive only if it renounces the right to be different, and integrates itself into the omnipotent realm of the profane.
3150.name: Theodor Adorno

3151.quote: The counterfeit and counterpart of Nature is reproduced in art.
3151.name: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

3152.quote: The most seductive thing about art is the personality of the artist himself.
3152.name: Paul Cezanne

3153.quote: The art of Peace I practice has room for each of the world's eight million gods, and I cooperate with them all. The God of Peace is very great and enjoins all that is divine and enlightened in every land.
3153.name: Morihei Ueshiba

3154.quote: I like it when somebody tells me a story, and I actually really feel that that's becoming like a lost art in American cinema.
3154.name: Quentin Tarantino

3155.quote: There's a lot of thought in art. People get to talk about important things. There's a lot of sex, you know, in art. There's a lot of naked women and men, and there's intrigue, there's fakery. It's a real microcosm of the larger world.
3155.name: Steve Martin

3156.quote: You want to be a bit compulsive in your art or craft or whatever you do.
3156.name: Steve Martin

3157.quote: I'm enamored with the art world. Anytime you look at anything that's considered artistic, there's a commercial world around it: the ballet, opera, any kind of music. It can't exist without it.
3157.name: Steve Martin

3158.quote: Art at its most significant is a Distant Early Warning System that can always be relied on to tell the old culture what is beginning to happen to it.
3158.name: Marshall McLuhan

3159.quote: Most works of art, like most wines, ought to be consumed in the district of their fabrication.
3159.name: Simone Weil

3160.quote: Art is why I get up in the morning but my definition ends there. You know I don't think its fair that I'm living for something I can't even define.
3160.name: Ani DiFranco

3161.quote: People believe that photographs are true and therefore cannot be art.
3161.name: Mason Cooley

3162.quote: Art seduces, but does not exploit.
3162.name: Mason Cooley

3163.quote: Art is the most beautiful deception of all. And although people try to incorporate the everyday events of life in it, we must hope that it will remain a deception lest it become a utilitarian thing, sad as a factory.
3163.name: Claude Debussy

3164.quote: To the man who loves art for its own sake, it is frequently in its least important and lowliest manifestations that the keenest pleasure is to be derived.
3164.name: Arthur Conan Doyle

3165.quote: Film will only became an art when its materials are as inexpensive as pencil and paper.
3165.name: Jean Cocteau

3166.quote: In art and dream may you proceed with abandon. In life may you proceed with balance and stealth.
3166.name: Patti Smith

3167.quote: Building art is a synthesis of life in materialised form. We should try to bring in under the same hat not a splintered way of thinking, but all in harmony together.
3167.name: Alvar Aalto

3168.quote: Skill without imagination is craftsmanship and gives us many useful objects such as wickerwork picnic baskets. Imagination without skill gives us modern art.
3168.name: Tom Stoppard

3169.quote: An art which isn't based on feeling isn't an art at all.
3169.name: Paul Cezanne

3170.quote: The knowledge of God is the cause of things. For the knowledge of God is to all creatures what the knowledge of the artificer is to things made by his art.
3170.name: Thomas Aquinas

3171.quote: I can't satisfy myself with just trying to tie all of my imagination into music, especially when music is not appreciated as an art form as much as it used to be.
3171.name: Marilyn Manson

3172.quote: Art gives me the freedom I don't have when I make music.
3172.name: Marilyn Manson

3173.quote: The idea is, if I can't heal from my art, then how can you heal?
3173.name: Maynard James Keenan

3174.quote: Riding a race bike is an art - a thing that you do because you feel something inside.
3174.name: Valentino Rossi

3175.quote: I try to keep a low profile in general. Not with my art, but just as a person.
3175.name: Alanis Morissette

3176.quote: In general it can be said that a nation's art is greatest when it most reflects the character of its people.
3176.name: Edward Hopper

3177.quote: At the University of Maryland, my first year I started off planning to major in art because I was interested in theatre design, stage design or television design.
3177.name: Jim Henson

3178.quote: What an artist is trying to do for people is bring them closer to something, because of course art is about sharing. You wouldn't be an artist unless you wanted to share an experience, a thought.
3178.name: David Hockney

3180.quote: Art is not what you see, but what you make others see.
3180.name: Edgar Degas

3181.quote: Design is the method of putting form and content together. Design, just as art, has multiple definitions there is no single definition. Design can be art. Design can be aesthetics. Design is so simple, that's why it is so complicated.
3181.name: Paul Rand

3182.quote: I don't have anything to say about other people's art and their work.
3182.name: Dolly Parton

3183.quote: Patience is the art of concealing your impatience.
3183.name: Guy Kawasaki

3184.quote: The screen is a magic medium. It has such power that it can retain interest as it conveys emotions and moods that no other art form can hope to tackle.
3184.name: Stanley Kubrick

3185.quote: For his heart was in his work, and the heart giveth grace unto every art.
3185.name: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

3187.quote: Art is a harmony parallel with nature.
3187.name: Paul Cezanne

3188.quote: Film as dream, film as music. No art passes our conscience in the way film does, and goes directly to our feelings, deep down into the dark rooms of our souls.
3188.name: Ingmar Bergman

3189.quote: I do not want art for a few any more than education for a few, or freedom for a few.
3189.name: William Morris

3190.quote: The style of ancient Egyptian art is transcendently clear, something 8-year-olds can recognize in an instant. Its consistency and codification is one of the most epic visual journeys in all art, one that lasts 30 dynasties spread over 3,000 years.
3190.name: Jerry Saltz

3191.quote: Egotism: The art of seeing in yourself what others cannot see.
3191.name: George V. Higgins

3192.quote: A work of art has no importance whatever to society. It is only important to the individual.
3192.name: Vladimir Nabokov

3193.quote: I don't think any movie or any book or any work of art can solve the stalemate in the Middle East today. But it's certainly worth a try.
3193.name: Steven Spielberg

3194.quote: I think that one's art is a growth inside one. I do not think one can explain growth. It is silent and subtle. One does not keep digging up a plant to see how it grows.
3194.name: Emily Carr

3195.quote: It is a sad fact about our culture that a poet can earn much more money writing or talking about his art than he can by practicing it.
3195.name: W. H. Auden

3196.quote: After a few months in my parents' basement, I took an apartment near the state university, where I discovered both crystal methamphetamine and conceptual art. Either one of these things are dangerous, but in combination they have the potential to destroy entire civilizations.
3196.name: David Sedaris

3197.quote: To know how to grow old is the master work of wisdom, and one of the most difficult chapters in the great art of living.
3197.name: Herman Melville

3198.quote: I had wanted a tape recorder since I was tiny. I thought it was a magic thing. I never got one until just before I went to art school.
3198.name: Brian Eno

3199.quote: It is not hard to understand modern art. If it hangs on a wall it's a painting, and if you can walk around it it's a sculpture.
3199.name: Tom Stoppard

3200.quote: Art is anything you can get away with.
3200.name: Marshall McLuhan

3201.quote: Everything a writer learns about the art or craft of fiction takes just a little away from his need or desire to write at all. In the end he knows all the tricks and has nothing to say.
3201.name: Raymond Chandler

3202.quote: Nature scarcely ever gives us the very best for that we must have recourse to art.
3202.name: Baltasar Gracian

3203.quote: To say nothing, especially when speaking, is half the art of diplomacy.
3203.name: Will Durant

3204.quote: Design in art, is a recognition of the relation between various things, various elements in the creative flux. You can't invent a design. You recognize it, in the fourth dimension. That is, with your blood and your bones, as well as with your eyes.
3204.name: David Herbert Lawrence

3205.quote: Oh literature, oh the glorious Art, how it preys upon the marrow in our bones. It scoops the stuffing out of us, and chucks us aside. Alas!
3205.name: David Herbert Lawrence

3206.quote: Everyone discusses my art and pretends to understand, as if it were necessary to understand, when it is simply necessary to love.
3206.name: Claude Monet

3207.quote: In its most limited sense, modern, art would seem to concern itself only with the technical innovations of the period.
3207.name: Edward Hopper

3208.quote: The question of the value of nationality in art is perhaps unsolvable.
3208.name: Edward Hopper

3209.quote: The trend in some of the contemporary movements in art, but by no means all, seems to deny this ideal and to me appears to lead to a purely decorative conception of painting.
3209.name: Edward Hopper

3210.quote: Life is short, the art long.
3210.name: Hippocrates

3211.quote: Everything that has ever been called folk art has always reflected domination.
3211.name: Theodor Adorno

3212.quote: Music is your own experience, your own thoughts, your wisdom. If you don't live it, it won't come out of your horn. They teach you there's a boundary line to music. But, man, there's no boundary line to art.
3212.name: Charlie Parker

3213.quote: My age and health will never allow me to realize the dream of art I've been pursuing all my life.
3213.name: Paul Cezanne

3214.quote: Don't be an art critic. Paint. There lies salvation.
3214.name: Paul Cezanne

3215.quote: Film editing is now something almost everyone can do at a simple level and enjoy it, but to take it to a higher level requires the same dedication and persistence that any art form does.
3215.name: Walter Murch

3216.quote: Love and business and family and religion and art and patriotism are nothing but shadows of words when a man's starving!
3216.name: O. Henry

3217.quote: It ought to be illegal for an artist to marry. If the artist must marry let him find someone more interested in art, or his art, or the artist part of him, than in him. After which let them take tea together three times a week.
3217.name: Ezra Pound

3218.quote: It is not in life, but in art that self-fulfillment is to be found.
3218.name: Wilson Mizner

3219.quote: Art lies by its own artifice.
3219.name: Ovid

3220.quote: Art has a double face, of expression and illusion, just like science has a double face: the reality of error and the phantom of truth.
3220.name: Publilius Syrus

3221.quote: Art and works of art do not make an artist sense and enthusiasm and instinct do.
3221.name: Karl Wilhelm Friedrich Schlegel

3222.quote: You can't but know that if you can capture the emotions of the audience as well as their minds, the play will work better, because it's a narrative art form.
3222.name: Tom Stoppard

3223.quote: Teachers believe they have a gift for giving it drives them with the same irrepressible drive that drives others to create a work of art or a market or a building.
3223.name: A. Bartlett Giamatti

3224.quote: The art challenges the technology, and the technology inspires the art.
3224.name: John Lasseter

3225.quote: To say the word Romanticism is to say modern art - that is, intimacy, spirituality, color, aspiration towards the infinite, expressed by every means available to the arts.
3225.name: Charles Baudelaire

3226.quote: What strikes me is the fact that in our society, art has become something which is only related to objects, and not to individuals, or to life.
3226.name: Michel Foucault

3227.quote: Art is so subjective, and people can react however they want.
3227.name: Jennifer Aniston

3228.quote: I'm free. I just do what I want, say what I want, say how I feel, and I don't try to hurt nobody. I just try to make sure that I don't compromise my art in any kind of way, and I think people respect that.
3228.name: Erykah Badu

3229.quote: Rumors sound of galleries asking artists for upsized art and more of it. I've heard of photographers asked to print larger to increase the wall power and salability of their work. Everything winds up set to maximum in order to feed the beast.
3229.name: Jerry Saltz

3230.quote: To engage with art, we have to be willing to be wrong, venture outside our psychic comfort zones, suspend disbelief, and remember that art explores and alters consciousness simultaneously.
3230.name: Jerry Saltz

3231.quote: Summer is a great time to visit art museums, which offer the refreshing rinse of swimming pools - only instead of cool water, you immerse yourself in art.
3231.name: Jerry Saltz

3232.quote: I can't bear art that you can walk round and admire. A book should be either a bandit or a rebel or a man in the crowd.
3232.name: David Herbert Lawrence

3233.quote: Since obscenity is the truth of our passion today, it is the only stuff of art - or almost the only stuff.
3233.name: David Herbert Lawrence

3234.quote: The essential function of art is moral. But a passionate, implicit morality, not didactic. A morality which changes the blood, rather than the mind.
3234.name: David Herbert Lawrence

3235.quote: I am more a friend of art than a producer of painting.
3235.name: Paul Cezanne

3236.quote: You say a new era in art is preparing you sensed it coming continue your studies without weakening. God will do the rest.
3236.name: Paul Cezanne

3237.quote: I have nothing to hide in art. The initial force alone can bring anyone to the end he must attain.
3237.name: Paul Cezanne

3238.quote: Is art really the priesthood that demands the pure in heart who belong to it wholly?
3238.name: Paul Cezanne

3239.quote: A frenzied passion for art is a canker that devours everything else.
3239.name: Charles Baudelaire

3240.quote: Evil is done without effort, naturally, it is the working of fate good is always the product of an art.
3240.name: Charles Baudelaire

3241.quote: I didn't grow up thinking of movies as film, or art, but as movies, something to do on a Saturday afternoon.
3241.name: Sydney Pollack

3242.quote: The art of living is the art of knowing how to believe lies.
3242.name: Cesare Pavese

3243.quote: Let's talk of a system that transforms all the social organisms into a work of art, in which the entire process of work is included, something in which the principle of production and consumption takes on a form of quality. It's a Gigantic project.
3243.name: Joseph Beuys

3244.quote: Any authentic work of art must start an argument between the artist and his audience.
3244.name: Rebecca West

3245.quote: History repeats itself, but the special call of an art which has passed away is never reproduced. It is as utterly gone out of the world as the song of a destroyed wild bird.
3245.name: Joseph Conrad

3246.quote: One of the most amazing things about mathematics is the people who do math aren't usually interested in application, because mathematics itself is truly a beautiful art form. It's structures and patterns, and that's what we love, and that's what we get off on.
3246.name: Danica McKellar

3247.quote: A rose is the visible result of an infinitude of complicated goings on in the bosom of the earth and in the air above, and similarly a work of art is the product of strange activities in the human mind.
3247.name: Clive Bell

3248.quote: It was Public Art, defined as art that is purchased by experts who are not spending their own personal money.
3248.name: Dave Barry

3249.quote: Art is not necessary at all. All that is necessary to make this world a better place to live in is to love - to love as Christ loved, as Buddha loved.
3249.name: Isadora Duncan

3250.quote: Advertising is fundamentally persuasion and persuasion happens to be not a science, but an art.
3250.name: William Bernbach

3251.quote: I was doing these performance art pop music pieces in the city. And they were a bit on the eccentric side I suppose. So people started to call me Gaga after the Queen song 'Radio Gaga.'
3251.name: Lady Gaga

3252.quote: Medicine is not only a science it is also an art. It does not consist of compounding pills and plasters it deals with the very processes of life, which must be understood before they may be guided.
3252.name: Paracelsus

3253.quote: I would no more quarrel with a man because of his religion than I would because of his art.
3253.name: Mary Baker Eddy

3254.quote: So long as the system of competition in the production and exchange of the means of life goes on, the degradation of the arts will go on and if that system is to last for ever, then art is doomed, and will surely die that is to say, civilization will die.
3254.name: William Morris

3255.quote: Poor Georgia O'Keeffe. Death didn't soften the opinions of the art world toward her paintings.
3255.name: Jerry Saltz

3256.quote: I've always said that an art critic can put aside politics around art.
3256.name: Jerry Saltz

3257.quote: Megacollectors suppose they can enter art history by spending astronomical amounts.
3257.name: Jerry Saltz

3258.quote: The art gods cooked up something special for James Ensor.
3258.name: Jerry Saltz

3259.quote: All art comes from other art, and all immigrants come from other places.
3259.name: Jerry Saltz

3261.quote: I have a soft spot for art that, in terms of subject matter and material, is in bad taste.
3261.name: Jerry Saltz

3262.quote: Art is changing. Again. Here. Now. Opportunities to witness this are rare, so attend and observe.
3262.name: Jerry Saltz

3263.quote: Art is good, bad, boring, ugly, useful to us or not.
3263.name: Jerry Saltz

3264.quote: Recessions are hard on people, but they are not hard on art.
3264.name: Jerry Saltz

3265.quote: I like that the art world isn't regulated.
3265.name: Jerry Saltz

3266.quote: The art world is molting - some would say melting. Galleries are closing museums are scaling back.
3266.name: Jerry Saltz

3267.quote: Almost all institutions own a lot more art than they can ever show, much of it revealing for its timeliness, genius, or sheer weirdness.
3267.name: Jerry Saltz

3268.quote: The forties, seventies, and the nineties, when money was scarce, were great periods, when the art world retracted but it was also reborn.
3268.name: Jerry Saltz

3269.quote: Robert Rauschenberg was not a giant of American art he was the giant. No American created so many aesthetic openings for so many artists.
3269.name: Jerry Saltz

3270.quote: The Met is not only the finest encyclopedic museum of art in the United States it is arguably the finest anywhere.
3270.name: Jerry Saltz

3271.quote: Money is something that can be measured art is not. It's all subjective.
3271.name: Jerry Saltz

3272.quote: Contrary to popular opinion, things don't go stale particularly fast in the art world.
3272.name: Jerry Saltz

3273.quote: Art usually only makes the news in America when the subject is money.
3273.name: Jerry Saltz

3275.quote: The price of a work of art has nothing to do with what the work of art is, can do, or is worth on an existential, alchemical level.
3275.name: Jerry Saltz

3276.quote: To me, nothing in the art world is neutral. The idea of 'disinterest' strikes me as boring, dishonest, dubious, and uninteresting.
3276.name: Jerry Saltz

3277.quote: The art world is an all-volunteer force. No one has to be here if he or she doesn't want to be, and we should be associating with anyone we want to.
3277.name: Jerry Saltz

3278.quote: Wolfgang Tillman's stunning large-scale pictures, being shown for the first time, were so offhand I failed to see them as art.
3278.name: Jerry Saltz

3279.quote: Galleries began growing in both number and size in the late seventies, when artists who worked in lofts wanted to exhibit their work in spaces similar to the ones the art was made in.
3279.name: Jerry Saltz

3280.quote: There's something pleasing about large, well-lit spaces. I love that dealers are willing to take massive chances in order to give this much room to their artists. Most of all, I love that more galleries showing more art gives more artists a shot.
3280.name: Jerry Saltz

3281.quote: First let me report that the art in the Barnes Collection has never looked better. My trips to the old Barnes were always amazing, but except on the sunniest days, you could barely see the art. The building always felt pushed beyond its capacity.
3281.name: Jerry Saltz

3282.quote: Not to say people shouldn't get rich from art. I adore the alchemy wherein artists who cast a complex spell make rich people give them their money. (Just writing it makes me cackle.) But too many artists have been making money without magic.
3282.name: Jerry Saltz

3283.quote: These days, newish art can be priced between $10,000 and $25,000. When I tell artists that a new painting by a newish artist should go for around $1,200, they look at me like I'm a flesh-eating virus.
3283.name: Jerry Saltz

3284.quote: In art, scandal is a false narrative, a smoke screen that camouflages rather than reveals. When we don't know what we're seeing, we overreact.
3284.name: Jerry Saltz

3285.quote: Damien Hirst is the Elvis of the English art world, its ayatollah, deliverer, and big-thinking entrepreneurial potty-mouthed prophet and front man. Hirst synthesizes punk, Pop Art, Jeff Koons, Marcel Duchamp, Francis Bacon, and Catholicism.
3285.name: Jerry Saltz

3286.quote: Anyone who relishes art should love the extraordinary diversity and psychic magic of our art galleries. There's likely more combined square footage for the showing of art on one New York block - West 24th Street between Tenth and Eleventh Avenues - than in all of Amsterdam's or Hamburg's galleries.
3286.name: Jerry Saltz

3287.quote: Yes, 85 percent of the art you see isn't any good. But everyone has a different opinion about which 85 percent is bad. That in turn creates fantastically unstable interplay and argument.
3287.name: Jerry Saltz

3288.quote: Many museums are drawing audiences with art that is ostensibly more entertaining than stuff that just sits and invites contemplation. Interactivity, gizmos, eating, hanging out, things that make noise - all are now the norm, often edging out much else.
3288.name: Jerry Saltz

3289.quote: Imagine it's 1981. You're an artist, in love with art, smitten with art history. You're also a woman, with almost no mentors to look to art history just isn't that into you. Any woman approaching art history in the early eighties was attempting to enter an almost foreign country, a restricted and exclusionary domain that spoke a private language.
3289.name: Jerry Saltz

3290.quote: Willem de Kooning is generally credited for coming out of the painterly gates strong in the forties, revolutionizing art and abstraction and reaching incredible heights by the early fifties, and then tailing off.
3290.name: Jerry Saltz

3291.quote: I also take pleasure in the so-called negative power in Grotjahn's work. That is, I love his paintings for what they are not. Unlike much art of the past decade, Grotjahn isn't simply working from a prescribed checklist of academically acceptable, curator-approved 'isms' and twists.
3291.name: Jerry Saltz

3292.quote: It is not possible to overstate the influence of Paul Cezanne on twentieth-century art. He's the modern Giotto, someone who shattered one kind of picture-making and invented a new one that the world followed.
3292.name: Jerry Saltz

3293.quote: The greatest work of art about New York? The question seems nebulous. The city's magic and majesty are distilled in the photographs of Alfred Stieglitz and Paul Strand.
3293.name: Jerry Saltz

3294.quote: Abstract Expressionism - the first American movement to have a worldwide influence - was remarkably short-lived: It heated up after World War II and was all but done for by 1960 (although visit any art school today and you'll find a would-be Willem de Kooning).
3294.name: Jerry Saltz

3295.quote: My culture-deprived, aspirational mother dragged me once a month from our northern suburb - where the word art never came up - to the Art Institute of Chicago. I hated it.
3295.name: Jerry Saltz

3296.quote: I'm noticing a new approach to art making in recent museum and gallery shows. It flickered into focus at the New Museum's 'Younger Than Jesus' last year and ran through the Whitney Biennial, and I'm seeing it blossom and bear fruit at 'Greater New York,' MoMA P.S. 1's twice-a-decade extravaganza of emerging local talent.
3296.name: Jerry Saltz

3297.quote: Outside museums, in noisy public squares, people look at people. Inside museums, we leave that realm and enter what might be called the group-mind, getting quiet to look at art.
3297.name: Jerry Saltz

3298.quote: It took the Metropolitan Museum of Art nearly 50 years to wake up to Pablo Picasso. It didn't own one of his paintings until 1946, when Gertrude Stein bequeathed that indomitable quasi-Cubistic picture of herself - a portrait of the writer as a sumo Buddha - to the Met, principally because she disliked the Museum of Modern Art.
3298.name: Jerry Saltz

3299.quote: All of Koons's best art - the encased vacuum cleaners, the stainless-steel Rabbit (the late-twentieth century's signature work of Simulationist sculpture), the amazing gleaming Balloon Dog, and the cast-iron re-creation of a Civil War mortar exhibited last month at the Armory - has simultaneously flaunted extreme realism, idealism, and fantasy.
3299.name: Jerry Saltz

3300.quote: Venice is the perfect place for a phase of art to die. No other city on earth embraces entropy quite like this magical floating mall.
3300.name: Jerry Saltz

3301.quote: Appropriation is the idea that ate the art world. Go to any Chelsea gallery or international biennial and you'll find it. It's there in paintings of photographs, photographs of advertising, sculpture with ready-made objects, videos using already-existing film.
3301.name: Jerry Saltz

3302.quote: After its hothouse incubation in the seventies, appropriation breathed important new life into art. This life flowered spectacularly over the decades - even if it's now close to aesthetic kudzu.
3302.name: Jerry Saltz

3303.quote: The New York art world readily proves people wrong. Just when folks say that things stink and flibbertigibbet critics wish the worst on us all because we're not pure enough, good omens appear.
3303.name: Jerry Saltz

3304.quote: Artistic qualities that once seemed undeniable don't seem so now. Sometimes these fluctuations are only fickleness of taste, momentary glitches in an artist's work, or an artist getting ahead of his audience (it took me ten years to catch up to Albert Oehlen). Other times, however, these problems mean there's something wrong with the art.
3304.name: Jerry Saltz

3305.quote: Can space break? I mean the space of art galleries. Over the past 100 years, art galleries have gone from looking like Beaux Arts salons to simple storefronts to industrial lofts to the gleaming giant white cubes of Chelsea with their shiny concrete floors.
3305.name: Jerry Saltz

3306.quote: It's great that New York has large spaces for art. But the enormous immaculate box has become a dated, even oppressive place. Many of these spaces were designed for sprawling installations, large paintings, and the Relational Aesthetics work of the past fifteen years.
3306.name: Jerry Saltz

3307.quote: The giant white cube is now impeding rather than enhancing the rhythms of art. It preprograms a viewer's journey, shifts the emphasis from process to product, and lacks individuality and openness. It's not that art should be seen only in rutty bombed-out environments, but it should seem alive.
3307.name: Jerry Saltz

3308.quote: It's art that pushes against psychological and social expectations, that tries to transform decay into something generative, that is replicative in a baroque way, that isn't about progress, and wants to - as Walt Whitman put it - 'contain multitudes.'
3308.name: Jerry Saltz

3309.quote: The last time money left the art world, intrepid types maxed out their credit cards and opened galleries, and a few of them have become the best in the world.
3309.name: Jerry Saltz

3310.quote: Much good art got made while money ruled I like a lot of it, and hardship and poverty aren't virtues. The good news is that, since almost no one will be selling art, artists - especially emerging ones - won't have to think about turning out a consistent style or creating a brand. They'll be able to experiment as much as they want.
3310.name: Jerry Saltz

3311.quote: While a large segment of the art world has obsessed over a tiny number of stars and their prices, an aesthetic shift has been occurring. It's not a movement - movements are more sure of themselves. It's a change of mood or expectation, a desire for art to be more than showy effects, big numbers, and gamesmanship.
3311.name: Jerry Saltz

3312.quote: When money and hype recede from the art world, one thing I won't miss will be what curator Francesco Bonami calls the 'Eventocracy.' All this flashy 'art-fair art' and those highly produced space-eating spectacles and installations wow you for a minute until you move on to the next adrenaline event.
3312.name: Jerry Saltz

3313.quote: A saboteur in the house of art and a comedienne in the house of art theory, Lawler has spent three decades documenting the secret life of art. Functioning as a kind of one-woman CSI unit, she has photographed pictures and objects in collectors' homes, in galleries, on the walls of auction houses, and off the walls, in museum storage.
3313.name: Jerry Saltz

3314.quote: Works of art often last forever, or nearly so. But exhibitions themselves, especially gallery exhibitions, are like flowers they bloom and then they die, then exist only as memories, or pressed in magazines and books.
3314.name: Jerry Saltz

3315.quote: If only we could persuade galleries to observe a fallow period in which, for two months every other year, new and old works of art could be sold in back rooms and all main galleries would be devoted to revisiting shows gone by.
3315.name: Jerry Saltz

3316.quote: A canon is antithetical to everything the New York art world has been about for the past 40 years, during which we went from being the center of the art world to being one of many centers.
3316.name: Jerry Saltz

3317.quote: It took me twenty years to get Steven Parrino's work. From the time I first saw his art, in the mid-eighties, I almost always dismissed it as mannered, Romantic, formulaic, conceptualist-formalist heavy-metal boy-art abstraction.
3317.name: Jerry Saltz

3318.quote: Another unsettling element in modern art is that common symptom of immaturity, the dread of doing what has been done before.
3318.name: Edith Wharton

3319.quote: Art is the signature of civilizations.
3319.name: Beverly Sills

3320.quote: Although all the good arts serve to draw man's mind away from vices and lead it toward better things, this function can be more fully performed by this art, which also provides extraordinary intellectual pleasure.
3320.name: Nicolaus Copernicus

3321.name: Arthur Erickson

3322.quote: Surrealism: An archaic term. Formerly an art movement. No longer distinguishable from everyday life.

3323.quote: I try to give people a different way of looking at their surroundings. That's art to me.
3323.name: Maya Lin

3324.quote: Translation is the art of failure.
3324.name: Umberto Eco

3325.quote: Life is very nice, but it lacks form. It's the aim of art to give it some.
3325.name: Jean Anouilh

3326.name: Nick Cave

3327.quote: Literature is the art of discovering something extraordinary about ordinary people, and saying with ordinary words something extraordinary.
3327.name: Boris Pasternak

3328.quote: Raising children is a creative endeavor, an art rather than a science.
3328.name: Bruno Bettelheim

3329.quote: The whole aspect of cinema and film festivals should be a moment to come together and celebrate art and humanity. It would be a shame if there was such a divide.
3329.name: Keanu Reeves

3330.quote: The art of economics consists in looking not merely at the immediate but at the longer effects of any act or policy it consists in tracing the consequences of that policy not merely for one group but for all groups.
3330.name: Henry Hazlitt

3331.quote: All art is exorcism. I paint dreams and visions too the dreams and visions of my time. Painting is the effort to produce order order in yourself. There is much chaos in me, much chaos in our time.

3332.name: David Hockney

3333.quote: Success and the art of making music are two different things for me.
3333.name: Norah Jones

3334.quote: People criticized me for my photography. They said it's not art.
3334.name: David Hockney

3335.quote: I always feel like the art's there and I just see it, so it's not really a lot of work.
3335.name: Damien Hirst

3336.quote: I went to art school actually when I was sixteen years old.
3336.name: David Hockney

3337.quote: How can anybody learn anything from an artwork when the piece of art only reflects the vanity of the artist and not reality?
3337.name: Lou Reed

3338.quote: Anyway I feel myself a bit on the edge on the art world, but I don't mind, I'm just pursuing my work in a very excited way. And there isn't really a mainstream anymore, is there?
3338.name: David Hockney

3339.quote: If you don't get noticed, you don't have anything. You just have to be noticed, but the art is in getting noticed naturally, without screaming or without tricks.
3339.name: Leo Burnett

3340.quote: It seems almost backwards to me that my music seems the more emotional outlet, and the art stuff seems more about ideas.
3340.name: David Byrne

3341.quote: Real popular culture is folk art - coalminers' songs and so forth.
3341.name: Noam Chomsky

3342.quote: I want to serve chess through games, books that are works of art. I would like to bring the game closer to many people all over the world.
3342.name: Garry Kasparov

3344.quote: In our life there is a single color, as on an artist's palette, which provides the meaning of life and art. It is the color of love.
3344.name: Marc Chagall

3345.quote: I want art to make me think. In order to do that, it may piss me off, or make me uncomfortable. That promotes awareness and change, or at least some discussion.
3345.name: Pink

3346.quote: Art is vice. You don't marry it legitimately, you rape it.
3346.name: Edgar Degas

3347.quote: Controversy is part of the nature of art and creativity.
3347.name: Yoko Ono

3348.quote: Oh yeah, I mean every fighter has got be dedicated, learn how to sacrifice, know what the devotion is all about, make sure you're paying attention and studying your art.
3348.name: Marvin Hagler

3349.quote: I am an anarchist in politics and an impressionist in art as well as a symbolist in literature. Not that I understand what these terms mean, but I take them to be all merely synonyms of pessimist.
3349.name: Henry Adams

3350.quote: The Dancer believes that his art has something to say which cannot be expressed in words or in any other way than by dancing.
3350.name: Doris Humphrey

3351.quote: Life is like art. You have to work hard to keep it simple and still have meaning.
3351.name: Charles de Lint

3352.quote: Ability is the art of getting credit for all the home runs somebody else hits.
3352.name: Casey Stengel

3353.quote: Interpretation is the revenge of the intellectual upon art.
3353.name: Susan Sontag

3354.quote: The 1990s, after the reign of terror of academic vandalism, will be a decade of restoration: restoration of meaning, value, beauty, pleasure, and emotion to art and restoration of art to its audience.

3356.quote: Because most of my career in the classroom has been at art schools (beginning at Bennington in the 1970s), I am hyper-aware of the often grotesque disconnect between commentary on the arts and the actual practice or production of the arts.
3356.name: Camille Paglia

3357.name: Camille Paglia

3358.name: Camille Paglia

3359.quote: It's high time for the art world to admit that the avant-garde is dead. It was killed by my hero, Andy Warhol, who incorporated into his art all the gaudy commercial imagery of capitalism (like Campbell's soup cans) that most artists had stubbornly scorned.
3359.name: Camille Paglia

3360.quote: To me, art supplies are always okay to buy.
3360.name: Louis C. K.

3361.quote: Art is something to be proud of. Art is no compromise.
3361.name: Christian Bale

3362.name: Wole Soyinka

3363.quote: The problem is that once the rules of art are debunked, and once the unpleasant realities the irony diagnoses are revealed and diagnosed, 'then' what do we do?

3364.name: Edward Koch

3365.quote: Courage is the art of being the only one who knows you're scared to death.
3365.name: Earl Wilson

3366.quote: The downfall of the industry seems to actually be good for art. I think the industry will find their way once the focus shifts from its greed-based origins, downsizes, and begins to support creative visions that speak to our times and shifting ideals.

3367.name: Paracelsus

3368.quote: The new job of art is to sit on the wall and get more expensive.

3369.quote: I am not a great cook, I am not a great artist, but I love art, and I love food, so I am the perfect traveller.
3369.name: Michael Palin

3370.quote: Art must take reality by surprise.
3370.name: Francoise Sagan

3371.quote: What you have now is a Hollywood that is pure poison. Hollywood was a central place in the history of art in the 20th century: it was human idealism preserved. And then, like any great place, it collapsed, and it collapsed into the most awful machinery in the world.

3372.quote: I have a small house so I borrow everything except art, that's what I love.
3372.name: Salma Hayek

3373.name: Maurice Sendak

3374.quote: I owe much to mother. She had an expert's understanding, but also approached art emotionally.
3374.name: David Rockefeller

3375.quote: For me, pointing and clicking my phone is absolutely fine. People say that isn't the art of photography but I don't agree.
3375.name: Annie Lennox

3376.quote: Art is the concrete representation of our most subtle feelings.
3376.name: Agnes Martin

3377.quote: Wisdom is nothing but a preparation of the soul, a capacity, a secret art of thinking, feeling and breathing thoughts of unity at every moment of life.
3377.name: Herman Hesse

3378.quote: For as long as I can remember I have suffered from a deep feeling of anxiety which I have tried to express in my art.
3378.name: Edvard Munch

3379.quote: If you cannot learn to love real art at least learn to hate sham art.
3379.name: William Morris

3380.quote: The greater the decrease in the social significance of an art form, the sharper the distinction between criticism and enjoyment by the public. The conventional is uncritically enjoyed, and the truly new is criticized with aversion.

3381.quote: Literature flourishes best when it is half a trade and half an art.
3381.name: William Ralph Inge

3382.quote: Fashion often starts off beautiful and becomes ugly, whereas art starts off ugly sometimes and becomes beautiful.
3382.name: David Bailey

3383.quote: The art of storytelling is reaching its end because the epic side of truth, wisdom, is dying out.
3383.name: Walter Benjamin

3384.quote: Art evokes the mystery without which the world would not exist.
3384.name: Rene Magritte

3385.quote: What matters poverty? What matters anything to him who is enamoured of our art? Does he not carry in himself every joy and every beauty?
3385.name: Sarah Bernhardt

3386.quote: Film is a very young art that is still evolving. Soon, we shall reach a balance between content and technology.
3386.name: Catherine Deneuve

3387.quote: All I owe the world is my art.
3387.name: Sherman Alexie

3388.quote: Art is dangerous. It is one of the attractions: when it ceases to be dangerous you don't want it.
3388.name: Duke Ellington

3389.quote: Aesthetic emotion puts man in a state favorable to the reception of erotic emotion. Art is the accomplice of love. Take love away and there is no longer art.
3389.name: Remy de Gourmont

3390.quote: When the bright angel dominates, out comes a great work of art, a Michelangelo David or a Beethoven symphony.
3390.name: Madeleine L'Engle

3391.quote: I like the fact that in ancient Chinese art the great painters always included a deliberate flaw in their work: human creation is never perfect.
3391.name: Madeleine L'Engle

3392.quote: I'm not dead and I don't have blue hair but some people say there are similarities. It is usually intolerable to watch myself onscreen but this time it's fine. I think it's beautiful and a real work of art.
3392.name: Helena Bonham Carter

3393.quote: More than art, more than literature, music is universally accessible.
3393.name: Billy Joel

3394.quote: I think no artist can claim to have any access to the truth, or an authentic version of an event. But obviously they have slightly better means at their disposal because they have their art to energize whatever it is they're trying to write about. They have music.
3394.name: Thom Yorke

3395.quote: Every man should follow the bent of his nature in art and letters, always provided that he does not offend against the rules of morality and good taste.
3395.name: Thomas Edward Brown

3396.quote: He has only half learned the art of reading who has not added to it the more refined art of skipping and skimming.
3396.name: Arthur Balfour

3397.quote: If only life could be a little more tender and art a little more robust.
3397.name: Alan Rickman

3398.quote: Seek art from every time and place, in any form, to connect with those who really move you.
3398.name: Martha Beck

3399.quote: Back then, I didn't have a big organization around me. I was just a kid with a guitar, traveling around. My responsibility basically was to the art, and I had extra time on my hands. There is no extra time now. There isn't enough time.
3399.name: Joni Mitchell

3400.quote: There's no being wrong in seeing something in art, only being disagreed with.
3400.name: Jonathan Safran Foer

3401.quote: The art of living does not consist in preserving and clinging to a particular mode of happiness, but in allowing happiness to change its form without being disappointed by the change happiness, like a child, must be allowed to grow up.
3401.name: Charles Morgan

3402.quote: I think good art does come from a dark place.
3402.name: Rick Springfield

3403.quote: I think of art as the highest level of creativity. To me, it is one of the greatest sources of enjoyment.
3403.name: David Rockefeller

3404.quote: Literature has drawn a funny perimeter that other art forms haven't.
3404.name: Jonathan Safran Foer

3405.quote: Reading is an art form, and every man can be an artist.
3405.name: Edwin Louis Cole

3406.quote: It is a myth that art has to be sold. It is not like stocking a grocery store where people fill a pushcart. Art is a product that has no apparent need. The salesperson builds the need in the mind of the buyer.
3406.name: Jack White

3407.quote: What I'm doing is art - it's low-brow art but there's a magic in that.
3407.name: Kesha

3408.quote: Art allows people a way to dream their way out of their struggle.
3408.name: Russell Simmons
